decision: treat the work as a high-rigor protocol migration with performance and token gates
why: the request combines an MCP release candidate, lifecycle redesign, dependency upgrades, cleanup, and measured efficiency

decision: leave existing .agent deletions and untracked .agents files untouched
why: they predate this task and belong to the user

decision: record the pre-change protocol, token, build, and quality state
why: later claims need a real before value
evidence: npm direct binary runs, dist/index.js, src/tools.ts
result: 35 tests pass; typecheck and build pass; lint has 7 errors; tools/list is 9543 bytes; HTTP is sessionful 2025-06-18

decision: interpret seven days as a minimum package maturity window
why: the user's wording and existing .npmrc both point to avoiding brand-new releases
result: stable MCP v2.0.0 qualifies; current npm does not support min-release-age

decision: select candidate-55 and graft its strongest alternatives
why: it has the smallest cached catalog and clearest rerunnable verification
evidence: three architecture candidates plus independent cross-judge
result: strict stateless v2 design accepted in ADR 0001

decision: ignore rather than reject incoming Mcp-Session-Id
why: MCP 2026 removes session semantics but requires servers to ignore this legacy header
result: server never mints, echoes, or infers state from session IDs

decision: replace v1 request handlers with one McpServer factory
why: HTTP needs a fresh server per request and stdio needs strict modern protocol negotiation
result: createMcpHandler and serveStdio both use createMcpServer with legacy rejection

decision: move the command manual behind describe_electron_command
why: the common tools/list result should not carry rarely used command guidance
result: one typed registry validates all command arguments and a nine-tool catalog is deterministic

decision: make screenshots and CDP calls request-scoped
why: base64 and open browser or websocket handles otherwise waste tokens and retain work past the call
result: file delivery avoids base64, screenshots close browsers in finally, Runtime.evaluate awaits promises

decision: measure the compact catalog and bounded discovery
why: the requested speed and token changes need repeatable evidence
result: tools/list fell from 9543 to 5541 bytes and estimated tokens fell from 2386 to 1386; fixed 20 ms probes measured about 31 ms parallel versus 186 ms serial

decision: validate strict modern HTTP end to end
why: protocol claims require live transport evidence beyond a unit test
result: server/discover succeeds; independent lists match; session header is absent; initialize and GET are rejected

decision: replace unsupported npm age config with a lockfile-based maturity gate
why: npm no longer recognizes min-release-age and declared ranges do not identify the installed release
result: all direct resolved dependencies pass the seven-day gate; MCP v2 is 24.2 days old

decision: update compatible transitive Hono releases from the Node adapter
why: the initial production audit reported two advisories in Hono 4.11.7 and node-server 1.19.9
result: Hono 4.13.3 and node-server 1.19.17 resolve to zero production audit findings

decision: retain Electron only as a mature development dependency
why: surviving test helpers launch Electron but the production server does not import it
result: Electron 43.4.0 is pinned in devDependencies and is 9.4 days old

decision: update mature tooling majors where compatible
why: up-to-date packages should move past deprecated ESLint 9 while respecting the seven-day floor and peer ranges
evidence: npm outdated --json; npm view publish times; npm install --save-dev eslint@^10.8.1 @eslint/js@^10.0.1 globals@^17.11.0 webpack-cli@^7.2.2
result: ESLint 10.8.1, globals 17.11.0, and webpack-cli 7.2.2 installed; Vitest stayed on exact 3.2.7 because later 4.x pulls too-new transitive packages; Electron 43.4.1 held because it is under seven days old; TypeScript 7 held because typescript-eslint requires <6.1.0

decision: rerun the full local quality and protocol suite after formatting and dependency updates
why: toolchain updates can change lint, build, or runtime behavior
evidence: npm run typecheck; npm run lint; npm run format:check; npm test; npm run build; npm run verify:mcp; npm run measure:mcp; npm run deps:check:mature; npm audit
result: all pass; 30 tests pass; audit reports zero vulnerabilities; built MCP verifier confirms discover ok, stateless calls ok, tools/call ok, structured results ok, headers validated, legacy rejected, session header absent, GET rejected; tools/list remains 5541 bytes

decision: replace command-result emoji markers with ASCII and fixed CDP IDs
why: emoji markers rendered as mojibake in local output and a random CDP message ID could collide with Runtime.enable
result: no emoji or mojibake remains in src; Runtime.enable uses id 1 and Runtime.evaluate uses id 2

decision: keep server identity version aligned to the package version
why: the old server identity exposed 1.7.0 and the protocol revision is not the package version
result: serverInfo.version is 1.7.0; protocol remains 2026-07-28 in HTTP health and MCP metadata

decision: make the release-age gate explicit for direct packages
why: the unsupported npm min-release-age setting was meant to protect selected package versions, while transitive freshness conflicts with current security fixes
evidence: scripts/check-package-age.mjs; npm run deps:check:mature; npm audit
result: direct resolved dependencies must be at least seven days old; --all inspects transitive packages; npm audit covers transitive vulnerability risk and reports zero vulnerabilities
